observations.finding: Call-plan construction is a major Java-stack and allocation hotspot in both principal runs.
observations.evidence: Exact JIRCallPlanBuilder.build frame: run-1 1459/2894 Java samples (50.415%) and 57,843,138,968 estimated allocated bytes (49.559%); run-2 453/845 samples (53.609%) and 28,155,178,048 bytes (61.547%).
observations.limits: These are overlapping inclusive Java-stack observations, not a prediction of equal wall-time savings. Broad FormsCache.withForm scopes include runtime callbacks and are not counted as construction.

observations.finding: Alias construction is substantial specifically in run-1.
observations.evidence: JIRCallPlanBuilder.aliases occurs in 759/2894 run-1 Java samples (26.227%). The constructor default alias callback _init_$lambda$0 is the nearest bidi allocation frame for 15,102,344,040 estimated bytes (12.939%).
observations.limits: No sampled arguments or per-plan cache counts identify which individual alias stages were later applied. _init_ method association with the default alias callback follows the sampled parent chain and source inspection.

observations.finding: Binding/normalizing sink rules accounts for much of run-2 allocation.
observations.evidence: JIRCallPlanBuilder.sinks is inclusive in 20,164,982,016 estimated run-2 allocated bytes (44.080%); normalizedSourceOrSink is nearest bidi site for 7,695,572,456 bytes (16.822%).
observations.limits: Inclusive sink/normalizer/builder weights overlap. Do not add them.

observations.finding: The run-2 sample does not identify demand lookup or summary pubsub as the leading Java-stack cost.
observations.evidence: Demand lookup/restriction families cover 8/845 Java samples (0.947%); summary pubsub 4/845 (0.473%). Return cleanup covers 41/845 (4.852%).
observations.limits: Java sampling may miss short frequent operations and native CPU. These shares do not prove those mechanisms are free or optimal.

observations.finding: Run-1 requests contain many repeated offered memberships, but profiles do not make them the leading sampled cost.
observations.evidence: 1,642,087 offered memberships; 82,957 fresh (5.052%); 1,335,643 temporary duplicates (81.338%); 223,487 authoritative duplicates (13.610%). Request-family Java share 79/2894 (2.730%).
observations.limits: Counters show duplicate work at the offer boundary. They do not imply storage retains duplicates or that removing all offers would improve total runtime proportionally.

algorithmic_followup_candidates.candidate: Defer alias-stage construction until an actual result passes the existing MemoryEffect guard.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.source: JIRCallPlanBuilder.build unconditionally calls aliases(back), while RunMethodCallServices.applyStage applies the guard before executing that stage.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.reason: An identity/no-effect result already skips alias application; it should not require expensive alias-edge construction if no later result uses that stage.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.required_check: Preserve prescan/static-operation metadata, resolver outcomes, resume stage identities, and every actual nonidentity path. Measure how many constructed stages are never used; profile alone does not give that ratio.

algorithmic_followup_candidates.candidate: Provide a cheap backward ZERO routing view before constructing full call rules and cleanup stages.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.source: RunMethodCallServices.process enters forms.withCall before zeroAtCall; full JIRCallPlanBuilder builds sinks, sources, cleanup, aliases and bindings for the call.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.reason: A backward ZERO with no local sink seed primarily needs callee/control routing. Existing target demand can reject callee ZERO admission before full rule materialization.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.required_check: Preserve real physical sink-seed binding paths, predefined summaries, unresolved zero-return behavior, and call resolution. Zero-only actor-step counters do not directly count ZERO fact steps.

algorithmic_followup_candidates.candidate: Measure call-form first builds versus rebuilds, then avoid repeated invariant rule-condition lowering if repetition is confirmed.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.source: FormsCache already caches a managed forward/reverse pair; JIRRuleForms.rewriteSourceOrSink normalizes and rewrites conditions on each construction.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.reason: Profiles establish heavy construction, not cache-miss duplication. An optimization should remove repeated construction or unused rule lowering, rather than merely speed up allocations.
algorithmic_followup_candidates.required_check: Enable existing form statistics in a separate approved experiment; do not infer cache failure from current wrappers or change SoftReferenceManager.
